title: AdS3 fixed-cutoff spacelike geodesic length
question: Does direct numerical integration of the bare spacelike geodesic arc length in a fixed Poincare AdS3 time slice reproduce its closed-form finite-cutoff length for endpoints at (±ell/2, epsilon)?

theory.object: A constant-t slice of Poincare AdS3 with metric ds^2=Lads^2*(dx^2+dz^2)/z^2, z>0.
theory.signature: Lorentzian AdS3 with signature (-,+,+); the fixed-time slice has the positive-definite hyperbolic metric shown in object.
theory.units: Coordinates x,z,epsilon and Lads have dimensions of length; the proper geodesic length also has dimension length. Ratios in the inverse hyperbolic sine and logarithm are dimensionless.
assumptions: Poincare patch at fixed coordinate time; the bulk metric and Lads are fixed.
Cutoff surface z=epsilon>0 and endpoints x=±ell/2, with fixed coordinate separation ell>0.
The relevant geodesic is the semicircle x^2+z^2=R^2 orthogonal to z=0, with R^2=(ell/2)^2+epsilon^2.
Only the bare finite-cutoff proper length is computed; no subtraction, Newton constant, replica calculation, or field-theory entropy is part of this example.
theory.boundary_conditions: At the chosen fixed time, geodesic endpoints are (x,z)=(-ell/2,epsilon) and (+ell/2,epsilon); ell=2 and Lads=1.5 are held fixed while epsilon varies over {0.02,0.01,0.005,0.0025,0.00125}.
theory.observable: The un-subtracted proper length of the spacelike geodesic between the two stated cutoff endpoints; its comparator is 2*Lads*asinh(ell/(2*epsilon)).
theory.regulator: A finite radial cutoff z=epsilon at both endpoints. This is a finite-cutoff observable, not an already renormalized length or an exact entropy.
theory.limit_order: Only a finite-epsilon sequence and a finite-difference UV-log diagnostic are shown. The epsilon-to-zero asymptotic is not taken as an exact finite-cutoff identity with a logarithm.
theory.normalization: Proper length from the displayed metric with fixed Lads; no division by 4G_N and no finite counterterm/subtraction. Keep fixed ell distinct from fixed geodesic circle radius.

claim.statement: For the declared finite cutoffs and fixed-coordinate-separation endpoints, adaptive numerical arc-length integration agrees with the closed-form bare geodesic length within the predeclared integration-error gate, while epsilon-halving differences diagnose the expected leading logarithmic coefficient.
claim.scope: One spacelike geodesic in a fixed Poincare AdS3 time slice with the listed ell, Lads and epsilon values; the UV coefficient is a finite-difference diagnostic only.
limitations: The numerical integrand and the closed form encode the same specified geodesic geometry; this is an implementation cross-check, not an independent proof of the holographic dictionary.
The cutoff is finite. No finite subtraction, renormalized observable, Newton constant, replica construction, or boundary CFT entropy is evaluated.
The calculation fixes coordinate endpoint separation ell. At fixed circle radius R, endpoint separation would instead be 2*sqrt(R^2-epsilon^2); these are different regulator paths.
forbidden_inferences: Do not call the computed finite-cutoff geodesic length an exact Ryu–Takayanagi entropy or an exact entanglement entropy.
Do not conflate fixed ell with fixed circle radius, or infer a physical CFT entropy without a justified holographic dictionary and normalization.

sources.revision: arXiv v2, last revised 7 March 2006; journal DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.181602.
sources.locator: arXiv bibliographic record and abstract read; Crossref journal metadata checked. Full paper derivation not read for this example.

protocol.disconfirming: Failure of a frozen numeric gate means this finite-cutoff quadrature/diagnostic did not meet its preregistered implementation criterion; it does not disprove a geodesic result, holography, or an entropy relation.
protocol.independence: The geometry, endpoints and observable are shared. The primary value is an adaptive Simpson integration of the induced line element after a stated parameter change; the comparator evaluates the elementary closed-form expression. These are distinct numerical/analytic implementations, not independent derivations of AdS/CFT or of the geodesic equation.
protocol.failure_interpretation: A script or quadrature error is an implementation failure. A metric miss is a finite numerical diagnostic miss. A pass checks only the stated finite-cutoff geometry and never promotes the length to an entropy or changes exploratory status.
